newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania sees 97 wheat output jumping to 8 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Romania sees 97 wheat output jumping to 8 mln T.

text.p: Romania hopes to bring in a wheat harvest of eight million tonnes this year, up from last year's figure of 3.1 million tonnes, and sees exports at 2.4 million tonnes, a farm ministry official said on Thursday.
"We estimate an unprecedented wheat crop of eight million tonnes and I think we could export some 2.4 million tonnes this year," Agriculture Ministry State Secretary Aurel Pana told Reuters.
Pana said the ministry had taken steps to help state-run and private mills and bakeries to buy part of the 1997 wheat crop by almost tripling the initial 550 billion lei earmarked for the operation.
"We issued an emergency decree to create a total fund of 1.4 trillion lei in credits for wheat purchases, so we are on the safe side," Pana said.
Last year Romania had a poor wheat crop of some 3.1 million tonnes due to bad weather and a late winter.
In 1995 Romania harvested 7.8 million tonnes and sold about 1.3 million.
Pana said Romania's wheat exports from the 1997 crop could amount to some 2.4 million tonnes.

"Domestic consumption is around five million tonnes, so theoretically we could export the balance," he said, but added, "Unfortunately, one should have in mind that our infrastructure allows only exports of up to 200,000 tonnes a month."
In 1995 Romania struggled to take full advantage of the bumper wheat crop and heavy foreign demand.
It struggled to move grain exports due to limited handling capacity at Constanta and an insufficient number of silos at its main Danube ports. Inadequate internal transport compounded the problem.
The Constanta silo has a capacity of 33,000 tonnes and can handle 6,000 tonnes a day.
A farm ministry source recently said Romania and the World Bank were considering plans to build a large capacity silo in the free trade area of the Constanta port.
Under the plan, local and foreign companies would build a silo with a storage capacity of 100,000 tonnes and the ability to handle 18,000 tonnes of grain a day.
Berths in the free trade area have a draft of 45 feet, which would allow access to ships of up to 30,000 dwt. The old silo can accommodate only ships of a maximum 10,000 dwt.
Constanta is also a strategic gateway into Europe, allowing access through the river network to the North Sea.
